$comment: Reviewed exceptions to the licence allowlist in check-licenses.mjs. Each entry matches one package name AND the exact licence string pnpm reports, so a licence change re-opens review. Blocked packages and forbidden licences (AGPL, GPL, SSPL, Elastic, BUSL, Commons Clause) cannot be listed here.

exceptions.reason: Font files bundled into the renderer. OFL-1.1 allows bundling and redistribution with software; it only bars selling the font on its own and reusing the reserved font name. It does not touch the licence of our code.

Monospace accessibility font bundled into the renderer as a terminal font option. Same OFL-1.1 terms as Inter and JetBrains Mono: redistribution with software is allowed, only standalone sale and reuse of the reserved font name are barred, and our code keeps its own licence.
Monospace font files bundled into the renderer. Same OFL-1.1 terms as Inter: redistribution with software is allowed and our code keeps its own licence.

Graph layout engine that beautiful-mermaid uses to lay out diagrams in chat-ui. EPL-2.0 is weak, file-level copyleft like MPL-2.0: we ship it unmodified and our code keeps its own licence. Any change to elkjs source files must be published under EPL-2.0.

Browser-support data table reached through browserslist and @babel/core, which @vanilla-extract/vite-plugin (a chat-ui production dependency) runs at build time. It is data, not code, and CC-BY-4.0 only requires the attribution its LICENSE file already carries.

package.json has no licence field, but the package ships a License file with the MIT text (Copyright (c) 2011 Felix Geisendörfer), checked 2026-09-10. Build-time only: reached through eval via @vanilla-extract/integration.
